title: Writing Cookie and the Army nickname
summary: Leclerc wrote Cookie while fooling at the piano. He served overseas about two years with the Washington Artillery as a sergeant first class, playing for singers and shows, and was nicknamed Cookie.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: How did you happen to write Cookie while I got you here?

Oh, I don't know. Just fooling around the piano. I used to play, you know, for the different places. And I did quite a bit of piano playing in the Army. I used to play for singers and little shows and things like that. And I guess I fooled around and just played it. Just...
Where were you in the Army?
Well, we first went to Little Rock. Then we went across. We were over there about two years.
Yeah. Was that the Washington artillery? Well, yeah. I left here with the Washington artillery in those days.
And what did you do? What was your job?
I was Sergeant First Class in those days, yeah.
Well, you didn't have to cook?
Huh? No, but I didn't. I played the piano. I said, you want me to do the...get out of doing this? I'll play the piano for you. Don't, I won't play the piano. I used to kid them, you know. Yeah.
Well, you weren't the...I thought they called you Cookie, I know.

Yeah, well, they called me Cookie on the kind of, you know, playing the number, you see. And of course, I used to sing it over there, too. And they all got to know it and sing it. And then they would have called me LeClaire. It was one of those things. Everywhere I went, they said, where's Cookie? Well, that was strange.
